title: “Getting the session history entries for the navigation API” drops rawEntries[0], breaking same-document traversal to the first entry

labels.name: compat
labels.description: Standard is not web compatible or proprietary feature needs standardizing

labels.name: topic: navigation API
labels.description: Topics directly related to the navigation API

body:
### What is the issue with the HTML Standard?

In [getting the session history entries for the navigation API](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/browsing-the-web.html#getting-session-history-entries-for-the-navigation-api), the loop in step 7 runs **While i > 0**. So it never visits `rawEntries[0]`. And so, when `startingIndex` is greater than 0, the first raw entry is dropped from `entriesForNavigationAPI` — even when it’s same-origin with the run.

That contradicts the assertion in [update the navigation API entries for a same-document navigation](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/nav-history-apis.html#update-the-navigation-api-entries-for-a-same-document-navigation) step 4.2: _“Assert: navigation’s current entry index is not -1.”_ If the first entry is same-origin and the user traverses back to it (a same-document traversal), [getting the navigation API entry index](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/nav-history-apis.html#getting-the-navigation-api-entry-index) returns -1, and the assertion fails. How to reproduce:

1. Load `https://example.com/` (becomes `rawEntries[0]`).
2. Navigate to a same-document fragment `#a` (`rawEntries[1]`).
3. Navigate cross-document to `/other` (`rawEntries[2]`).
4. Traverse back twice.

The 2nd back is a same-document traversal to `rawEntries[0]` — whose entry index is -1 because it was omitted — so, step 4.2 asserts.

So the spec should be fixed such that step 7 is changed instead to **While i ≥ 0**.

Step 7.1 already breaks before a cross-origin initial entry — so descending to index 0 only adds entries that actually belong in the list.

### Implementations

I ran across this when investigating a Ladybird crash, https://github.com/LadybirdBrowser/ladybird/issues/8700, and patching it in https://github.com/LadybirdBrowser/ladybird/pull/10380.

I then looked at the Blink code and found that Blink’s `PopulateSingleNavigationApiHistoryEntryVector` already does exactly the same thing I ending up doing for Ladybird: It violates the current spec and iterates with `i >= 0` (down to and including index 0).
